# Architecture

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## Actual-state governance

### Decision

Use a status-gated source-record system: published notes generate README; approved requests generate PRD; accepted decisions generate ARCHITECTURE; active rules generate AGENTS. The generated files are deterministic, committed and never edited separately.

Repository documents describe **only current tracked/observed capabilities**. Implementation designs, API shapes, data schemas, target diagrams and future rules belong only in GitHub issues, not in generated PRD or architectural records.

### Consequences

Every PR with an implementation or governance change updates the affected source records, regenerates all affected outputs, checks their exactness, and labels any unverified external behavior BLOCKED rather than IMPLEMENTED.

_Source: [0001-source-records.md](decisions/0001-source-records.md)_


## Native directories and repository-owned tests

### Decision

Keep independent physical `.github/` and `.agents/` directories, the repository's entire test suite under `.github/tests/`, roles and skills in `.agents/agents/` and `.agents/skills/`, and the existing repository-owned `.darkfactory/installation.json` integration metadata. Distinguish historical assignment references from diagrams generated from actual source. Proposed implementation diagrams live in issues, not in `.agents/requirements/`.

### Consequences

GitHub Actions remains natively discoverable; there is no mirrored test, workflow, DarkFactory source or speculative API/SQL/JSON authority.

_Source: [0002-layout.md](decisions/0002-layout.md)_


## Actual branch and review controls

### Decision

A `develop` branch now exists at the previous `main` commit, preserving the complete working tree and PR ancestry. GitHub still advertises the protected `main` branch as its default; the owner has now directed that `develop` become the default and integration branch, with `main` reserved for reviewed release promotion. This PR records that requested target but does not claim the GitHub setting has already changed. Implementation PRs remain issue-bound and require independent maintainer review and explicit approval of their final revisions. Passing CI is necessary but not sufficient.

### Consequences

The fork-source common ancestor has been verified as `a98e36d098a1ee9aa3e793cfc39040ad6e6d2e4e` and preserved by the `release/fork-base` branch. This repository commit includes a native `main-source` gate that rejects release PRs not originating from the same repository's `develop`; native branch protection must **require** its `main-source` check and enforce approvals to make this effective. An administrator must set GitHub's actual default branch to `develop` as requested. This also keeps default-branch-only issue, schedule, and manually dispatched workflows on the integration branch when the fork-base release `main` is introduced. The release-only policy separately depends on live branch protection and the required `main-source` workflow. Approval of each `develop` → `main` PR is the authorization to trigger the normal main-push release.

_Source: [0003-review.md](decisions/0003-review.md)_


## Versioning and release ownership

### Decision

`repo.dfconfig` uses DarkFactory PrideVer; no separate tag-only or `VERSION`-file authority should be installed. The tracked `.github/workflows/release.yml` automatically publishes the DarkFactory PrideVer GitHub Release when the protected `main` branch advances, including after a reviewed merge from `develop`. It also permits explicit manual dispatch on `main`. Read-only pull-request validation does not release. Publication checks the exact live main HEAD and rejects tag reuse across different commits.

### Consequences

The approved `develop` → `main` merge supplies the release authorization; no second manual release command is required. Main protection must include the `main-source` status check, independent approval, strict up-to-date checking, required conversation resolution and administrator enforcement. Declaring these rules in `repo.dfconfig` alone does not change GitHub's provider state; the release topology becomes enforceable only after the pending admin cutover and protection application.

_Source: [0004-release.md](decisions/0004-release.md)_


## Implemented source boundaries

### Decision

The checked-in Python source under `packages/engine/` owns its app entry point, controller and models; chess and checkers JSON assets live under their respective `packages/` directories. Documentation building and GitHub workflow automation live in `.github/`. Source-derived Mermaid diagrams represent those tracked source declarations.

### Consequences

No client app, FastAPI multiplayer lifecycle, Supabase schema, declarative engine contract, or native distribution is implemented by this governance PR. Proposed application architecture and acceptance criteria are tracked in the [unified master issue #348](https://github.com/marius-patrik/BoardGamesWithQuests/issues/348), to be documented in-repo only when corresponding code lands.

_Source: [0005-existing-code.md](decisions/0005-existing-code.md)_


## Portable agent roles and skills

### Decision

Keep the five repository-local roles (orchestrator, planner, implementer, reviewer and verifier) in `.agents/agents/` and task-focused procedures in `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. All roles inherit generated `.agents/AGENTS.md`; procedures supplement rather than override approved requirements, human review or security controls.

### Consequences

These Markdown records are portable guidance, not a competing agent runtime. They do not prove a particular execution provider has discovered, installed or invoked a role or skill. Review and verification require reproducible evidence before a maintainer authorizes merge.

_Source: [0006-agent-roles-and-skills.md](decisions/0006-agent-roles-and-skills.md)_
